OTHER END STATES · 51
OTHER 1
vera_ledger
filed jan_fate
recanted tomas_gate
passed
assuming in circle · kastan loyal · route watched · rybar vindictive
  1. A slip arrives in the intake tray before the tea urn is hot: the District Register is to be reconciled in full before the inspection from Central. Every serial a folder, every folder its white. The slip is unsigned, which means the corridor. Berta pins it to the Plan Calendar, and the Plan Calendar says Week 40.
    Ops. IV to Records IV: District Register to be reconciled in full before Central inspection. All serials.
  2. The admissions file for the medical faculty is a thin folder with a blue tab and a card clipped to the front. Rybar unclips the card and writes on the back, in the corridor's hand, one line: review held pending completion of household file, Records IV. He initials it and clips it back. He telephones nobody. The card goes back to the faculty by the morning courier, and the faculty files it, and the faculty secretary types a note to the applicant's mother's address, which is also the applicant's. The note arrives on a Tuesday. It is very short and it says pending.
    Faculty adm. card, HALM Ilona: REVIEW HELD, pending completion of household file IV/7781/R.40, Records IV. R.
  3. The form is called a Statement of Position and has a place for a signature and a place for particulars. The particulars are the point. Ilona writes that she attended, that she did not know the nature, that she renounces. Then the line asks where, and the pen stops, and she writes the street, the number, and the word cellar. Her handwriting is her mother's, slightly. The registrar reads it without expression and says the committee can sit again this week. On the stair at home the light clicks off, and she does not press it, and goes up in the dark to flat 5.
    Statement of Position, HALM Ilona: attendance admitted, renounced. Particulars: Vrba 9, cellar, press. Resit.
  4. The Tuesday international is on the bridge at 14:10, nine cars and the staff compartment. The attendant stands in the corridor with his railway card out and a parcel on the shelf behind his head, brown paper, a chemist's string. The dogs are on the platform. The company starts at car one. The log is open on a knee.
    Brenava log, Tues.: 14:10 intl., 9 cars + staff. Inspection begun. O.P.
  5. The staff compartment is last. Marek has his railway card in his hand and the parcel on the shelf behind his head, brown paper, chemist's string. Tomas looks at the card, and at the parcel, and at the parcel. The dogs are on the platform, fed. Ondra is on the step with the log open. "Clear," Tomas says, and stamps the card, and the stamp is the right one. The compartment is not in the log as opened, because it was not opened. The train pulls off the bridge at 14:19. Ondra's pen is still over the line. There is a line in the log with nothing after the time.
    Brenava log, Tues. 14:10 intl.: cars 1-9 insp. Staff compt.: [blank]. O.P.
  6. Two knocks on the hatch, a pause, one knock. Marek comes down the ladder backwards with the bag against his chest, still in the railway coat. On the bench he sets out what the staff compartment carried for the press: two reams of thin Western stock and a tin of ink. The smaller parcel, brown paper and a Vienna chemist's string, stays in his coat. "Flat 3," Marek says. "Before she books the call." Jan weighs the reams the way the press weighs them: four hundred sheets, eight readers a sheet. The cellar has paper again. Marek is already on the ladder, and goes up by the stair. He never sits.
    Lis cellar tally (pencil, beam): stock in, 2 rm. Ink, 1.
  7. The room at the Ribbon has a table, two chairs and a typewriter whose sample page is on file. Rybar does not raise his voice; he has not needed to. The declaration is already typed. Jan reads it. It says that he, Jan Rusek, published without licence, that the publication was unauthorised and its contents untrue, that he regrets. It does not ask for names, which is the kindness. He signs. The pen is the state's. It goes through two carbons, white and pink, and the pink stays on the table where he can see it. "Thank you," says Rybar, and means the signature.
    Declaration, RUSEK Jan: publication unlicensed, contents untrue. Regret expressed. Signed. Copies 2.
  8. The building book sits on the lodge ledge and Kastan writes in it in pencil. Tonight's entry: the hour, the landing, a figure at the door of flat 3 after the gate was barred, how long, which flat the figure went up to. He writes it as he saw it from the third-floor rail: a coat, a knuckle on the door, no light. He does not write what was said, because he did not hear. Thursday he copies the line onto the handler's form and the handler asks nothing. The line goes into a folder whose subject is the widow, and across to a card whose subject is not.
    Source RIBA, W40: 23:10, HALM V. (5) at door of 3, approx. 1 min, no light. Cross-ref. IV/7781/R.40.
  9. The string tie comes undone in two pulls. Form K-1, then forty leaves numbered in the corner by a hand that changed twice in nine years. Vera reads as the office reads: cover, index, last leaf first. Leaf 40 is a source report, two lines and a foot. A parcel carried up the stair on a Tuesday by a man in a railway coat. Contents stated as medicine, foreign. At the foot, a source and a receipt number. The stair is Vrba Street, number 9; the flat is 3, a widow's. Vera knows the stair. She knows the cough through the wall. She closes the folder on her thumb to keep the place, and the tab stripe is red.
    IV/4471/R.31 leaf 40. Source report, fond S: parcel up stair to Vrba 9/3, Tues., rail staff. Stated: medicine, foreign.
  10. Vera uncaps the ink and opens the District Register to the next free line. The pen is the office's; the hand is hers. Serial, year opened, subject, address, status. The line takes eleven seconds and makes no sound but the nib. She blots it. Then the cross-reference, fond S, a codename and a receipt number, so that the one who told is paid. Then the household card, tab turned from pending to complete. She ties the folder with the corridor's double knot and sets it in the out tray, where Berta's eyes will pass over it and not stop. The ledger balances. Nothing in the room has changed except the line.
    Register leaf 212 line 14. IV/4471/R.31 SOKOL Marta, Vrba 9/3. ACTIVE, observation. Ref. fond S/RIBA, rcpt 118.
  11. A card arrives at flat 5 by the morning post, faculty crest, typed: the admissions review will sit this week. Date, room, no time. The card has a line for household file, and the line has been filled in by somebody else, in a hand from an office. Vera puts it on the table and Ilona reads it without picking it up.
    Faculty notice: adm. review to sit this week, HALM Ilona. Household file IV/7781/R.40: see attached.
  12. A car from the Ribbon is at the post by eight. A captain in a civilian coat asks for the log, a room and a cup of tea, in that order, and is given all three. The company stands outside the guardroom in the sand and is called in one at a time, and the ones who come out do not say what was asked.
    4th Bn. Brenava: inquiry convened, gate log W40. All gate personnel to attend. Ops. IV.
  13. The review sits in a room at the faculty with a long table and a Plan Calendar. The chair reads the file aloud, which is how a decision is made: name, household, the card from the Records Office with its one line on the back, the Statement of Position if there is one, the marks. The marks are good. A man from the corridor sits at the end of the table, says nothing, and is not introduced. The chair says admitted, the secretary writes it, and the stamp comes down. The letter is typed the same afternoon. In flat 5 it is read standing up, twice, and put in the drawer.
    Faculty adm. review, HALM Ilona: ADMITTED, medical faculty, R.40. File closed, blue tab.
  14. The captain is polite. He lays the log on the table between them, open at the line with nothing after the time, and does not point. "I'm not interested in the line," he says. "I'm interested in what comes through it." Ondra is at the door with his cap under his arm. Tomas has seen the parcel on the shelf, the chemist's string, the railway card. He says what the parcel was, whose coat carried it, and which day of the week. The captain writes it down and underlines the day. The log closes. Ondra is told to go back to the stool. Nobody says his name again.
    4th Bn. report, Brenava: supply route: Tues. intl. train, rail staff, parcels, Vienna. Log clerk cleared.

  1. The list at Brenava is a sheet pinned inside the stamp cabinet, retyped weekly. Rybar adds to it by telephone, reading slowly, and the company clerk types what he reads: the Tuesday international, staff compartment, railway attendants by name, parcels addressed to District IV, Lom. The clerk reads it back. "Thank you," Rybar says, and rings off, and the line stays open half a second. At the gate the sheet goes up with a new line at the bottom and the conscripts read it at the start of the shift the way they read the weather. Seventy kilometres away, a widow's Tuesday has been retyped.
    Brenava list, W40 add.: Tues. intl. train, staff compt., rail attendants: OPEN ALL. Parcels to Lom IV: SEIZE.
  2. A slip arrives in the intake tray before the tea urn is hot: the District Register is to be reconciled in full before the inspection from Central. Every serial a folder, every folder its white.   5. The staff compartment is last. Marek has his railway card in his hand and the parcel on the shelf behind his head, brown paper, chemist's string. Tomas looks at the card, and at the parcel, and at the parcel. The dogs are on the platform, fed. Ondra is on the step with the log open. "Clear," Tomas says, and stamps the card, and the stamp is the right one. The compartment is not in the log as opened, because it was not opened. The train pulls off the bridge at 14:19. Ondra's pen is still over the line. There is a line in the log with nothing after the time.
    Brenava log, Tues. 14:10 intl.: cars 1-9 insp. Staff compt.: [blank]. O.P.
  6. The stove in the banking hall is lit from October. Vera carries the folder across the room at the pace of someone going for tea. Forty leaves, numbered in the corner, go in by fours. The carbons curl first, violet, then white. The K-1 board cover she keeps, because a cover is not a report. Nobody looks up; the urn is loud. Back at the desk the intake log shows a serial with no leaf count beside it, and the initials against that line are not hers. Berta signed the folder in this morning. Vera uncaps her pen and does not write anything.
    Intake log, Mon.: IV/4471/R.31 received, B.L. Leaves: [blank]. Out: [blank].
  7. The telephone in flat 5 rings at nine, which is the corridor's hour. The line hums louder than it should. "Comrade Halm. Rybar, Operations." Polite, unhurried, a man with a cup of tea. "Report four-four-seven-one, year thirty-one. It is active and I have the pink. Central does not have the white. Where is it in the Register." A question without a question mark. Vera says she will look in the morning. "The morning, then," he says. "Thank you." The soft double click; the line stays open half a second after she sets it down. Ilona, at the table, has stopped writing.
    Ops. IV, Rybar, call log: HALM V., re IV/4471/R.31, location in Register queried. Reply due a.m.
  8. The violet carbon of leaf 40 is still in the district, because the district keeps everything. Vera signs for the carbon box, finds the source report by serial, and types the leaf back onto office stock through two fresh carbons, with the margin slightly wrong. A folder with a missing leaf is a gap; a folder with a retyped leaf is a folder. She numbers it in the corner in the hand the index already shows, and writes the leaf count into the intake log where the line was blank. Berta's initials stay beside it. The ledger will balance tonight. Vera washes the ink from her thumb.
    Intake log: IV/4471/R.31, leaves 40, reconstituted from district carbon. V.H.
  9. A card arrives at flat 5 by the morning post, faculty crest, typed: the admissions review will sit this week. Date, room, no time. The card has a line for household file, and the line has been filled in by somebody else, in a hand from an office. Vera puts it on the table and Ilona reads it without picking it up.
    Faculty notice: adm. review to sit this week, HALM Ilona. Household file IV/7781/R.40: see attached.
  10. The review sits in a room at the faculty with a long table and a Plan Calendar. The chair reads the file aloud, which is how a decision is made: name, household, the card from the Records Office with its one line on the back, the Statement of Position if there is one, the marks. The marks are good. A man from the corridor sits at the end of the table, says nothing, and is not introduced. The chair says admitted, the secretary writes it, and the stamp comes down. The letter is typed the same afternoon. In flat 5 it is read standing up, twice, and put in the drawer.
    Faculty adm. review, HALM Ilona: ADMITTED, medical faculty, R.40. File closed, blue tab.
  11. Two knocks on the hatch, a pause, one knock. Marek comes down the ladder backwards with the bag against his chest, still in the railway coat. On the bench he sets out what the staff compartment carried for the press: two reams of thin Western stock and a tin of ink. The smaller parcel, brown paper and a Vienna chemist's string, stays in his coat. "Flat 3," Marek says. "Before she books the call." Jan weighs the reams the way the press weighs them: four hundred sheets, eight readers a sheet. The cellar has paper again. Marek is already on the ladder, and goes up by the stair. He never sits.
    Lis cellar tally (pencil, beam): stock in, 2 rm. Ink, 1.
  12. The platen comes down and the house takes the sound through its floor. Jan sets the type by lamp: two columns, the masthead cut from lino, the week's sheet. Ink on the roller, roller on the chase, sheet in, sheet out, the right margin smudged where the roller always runs dry. He stops reading what he prints after the first fifty; the hands know it. Stove cold, lamp low, the tram bell at the loop at half past four. By first light the stack under the beam is four hundred, uneven, inked wrong, people's paper. He wipes his hands on the rag and the hands stay black.
    Lis cellar tally: run 400. Stock out, 1 rm. Sheet W40.
  13. Thursday is the meeting. The handler has a corner table at the baths cafe and a receipt book with a carbon. Kastan gives the week: the gate round, who pressed the stair light after ten, which flat has the radio tuned west, who came up the stair with a parcel and on which day. He gives it the way he keeps the building book: by the hour. The handler writes, turns the book, and Kastan signs for a sum that would not buy a coat. The sum is not the point; the signature is. He gets two packets of cigarettes with it, which is the custom, and goes home on tram 11.
    Receipt book IV/S, no. 118: source RIBA, W40, paid, signed. Report filed to IV/4471/R.31 and IV/7781/R.40.
  14. The search has a form and the form has an inventory. Rybar comes down the ladder last, after the two in overalls, and touches nothing. He reads the beam where the tally is pencilled. The press is listed by its maker's plate; the type by the case; the stock by the ream; the sheets by the count. Jan stands by the stove with his hands black and is asked, politely, to sign the inventory as present. He signs. The hatch is sealed with a paper seal that carries the Drawer. The chestnut drops a leaf on it. Jan goes up the ladder between the two in overalls.
    Search inventory, Vrba 9 cellar: platen press (1), type cases (3), stock, sheets. Present: RUSEK J. Sealed.

  9. The pink carbon goes to the handling officer, the white to Central, the violet stays. Vera has, for one evening, all three on her desk, and the count in the carbon box is Berta's to keep. She folds the violet of leaf 40 into the back of a Plan Calendar sheet, slogan outward, and puts it in her coat. On Vrba Street the cellar hatch is under the chestnut, which the third floor cannot see. She does not go down. She leaves the folded sheet under the bin lid where paper for the press is left, and goes up to flat 5, and runs the tap.
    Carbon box, district: IV/4471/R.31 leaf 40, violet. Count 0 of 1. Checked B.L.
  10. The older signatories want names printed; the wall-writers want none. Jan sets the name himself, so that nobody else has set it. Third floor, front, caretaker since 1984, a telephone in one year instead of eight, a source with a receipt. Beneath it, as proof, the line from a source report, with the receipt number left on, in the state's own wording, serial and all. Four hundred copies. One sheet is read by eight. One of the eight will be the corridor, and the corridor will know which office the serial came from. Jan prints it anyway. The press does not care whose name it is.
    Ops. IV: Lis W40 col. 2 recovered. Quotes IV/4471/R.31 leaf 40 verbatim. Source office: Records IV. Trace by desk.

  14. The question is asked once, politely, and then the room waits. The inventory from the cellar is on the table: two reams of thin Western stock, a tin of ink, a chemist's string. "The paper is foreign. Somebody carries it." Jan looks at the string for a long time. Then he gives the name that is already on the railway's staff roster and the Tuesday train's duty sheet, where they could have found it in an hour. "Marek. The sleeping car." Rybar writes it in a hand that does not hurry. The string stays on the table. The train is due on the bridge at 14:10.
    Statement RUSEK J., add.: supply via rail staff, Tues. intl. train, attendant MAREK. To list, Brenava.

    Faculty adm. card, HALM Ilona: REVIEW HELD, pending completion of household file IV/7781/R.40, Records IV. R.
  7. The form is called a Statement of Position and has a place for a signature and a place for particulars. The particulars are the point. Ilona writes that she attended, that she did not know the nature, that she renounces. Then the line asks where, and the pen stops, and she writes the street, the number, and the word cellar. Her handwriting is her mother's, slightly. The registrar reads it without expression and says the committee can sit again this week. On the stair at home the light clicks off, and she does not press it, and goes up in the dark to flat 5.
    Statement of Position, HALM Ilona: attendance admitted, renounced. Particulars: Vrba 9, cellar, press. Resit.
  8. The violet carbon of leaf 40 is still in the district, because the district keeps everything. Vera signs for the carbon box, finds the source report by serial, and types the leaf back onto office stock through two fresh carbons, with the margin slightly wrong. A folder with a missing leaf is a gap; a folder with a retyped leaf is a folder. She numbers it in the corner in the hand the index already shows, and writes the leaf count into the intake log where the line was blank. Berta's initials stay beside it. The ledger will balance tonight. Vera washes the ink from her thumb.
    Intake log: IV/4471/R.31, leaves 40, reconstituted from district carbon. V.H.
  9. Two knocks on the hatch, a pause, one knock. Marek comes down the ladder backwards with the bag against his chest, still in the railway coat. On the bench he sets out what the staff compartment carried for the press: two reams of thin Western stock and a tin of ink. The smaller parcel, brown paper and a Vienna chemist's string, stays in his coat. "Flat 3," Marek says. "Before she books the call." Jan weighs the reams the way the press weighs them: four hundred sheets, eight readers a sheet. The cellar has paper again. Marek is already on the ladder, and goes up by the stair. He never sits.
    Lis cellar tally (pencil, beam): stock in, 2 rm. Ink, 1.
  10. A card arrives at flat 5 by the morning post, faculty crest, typed: the admissions review will sit this week. Date, room, no time. The card has a line for household file, and the line has been filled in by somebody else, in a hand from an office. Vera puts it on the table and Ilona reads it without picking it up.
    Faculty notice: adm. review to sit this week, HALM Ilona. Household file IV/7781/R.40: see attached.
  11. The review sits in a room at the faculty with a long table and a Plan Calendar. The chair reads the file aloud, which is how a decision is made: name, household, the card from the Records Office with its one line on the back, the Statement of Position if there is one, the marks. The marks are good. A man from the corridor sits at the end of the table, says nothing, and is not introduced. The chair says admitted, the secretary writes it, and the stamp comes down. The letter is typed the same afternoon. In flat 5 it is read standing up, twice, and put in the drawer.
    Faculty adm. review, HALM Ilona: ADMITTED, medical faculty, R.40. File closed, blue tab.
  12. The list at Brenava is a sheet pinned inside the stamp cabinet, retyped weekly. Rybar adds to it by telephone, reading slowly, and the company clerk types what he reads: the Tuesday international, staff compartment, railway attendants by name, parcels addressed to District IV, Lom. The clerk reads it back. "Thank you," Rybar says, and rings off, and the line stays open half a second. At the gate the sheet goes up with a new line at the bottom and the conscripts read it at the start of the shift the way they read the weather. Seventy kilometres away, a widow's Tuesday has been retyped.
    Brenava list, W40 add.: Tues. intl. train, staff compt., rail attendants: OPEN ALL. Parcels to Lom IV: SEIZE.
  13. The pink carbon goes to the handling officer, the white to Central, the violet stays. Vera has, for one evening, all three on her desk, and the count in the carbon box is Berta's to keep. She folds the violet of leaf 40 into the back of a Plan Calendar sheet, slogan outward, and puts it in her coat. On Vrba Street the cellar hatch is under the chestnut, which the third floor cannot see. She does not go down. She leaves the folded sheet under the bin lid where paper for the press is left, and goes up to flat 5, and runs the tap.
    Carbon box, district: IV/4471/R.31 leaf 40, violet. Count 0 of 1. Checked B.L.
  14. The older signatories want names printed; the wall-writers want none. Jan sets the name himself, so that nobody else has set it. Third floor, front, caretaker since 1984, a telephone in one year instead of eight, a source with a receipt. Beneath it, as proof, the line from a source report, with the receipt number left on, in the state's own wording, serial and all. Four hundred copies. One sheet is read by eight. One of the eight will be the corridor, and the corridor will know which office the serial came from. Jan prints it anyway. The press does not care whose name it is.
    Ops. IV: Lis W40 col. 2 recovered. Quotes IV/4471/R.31 leaf 40 verbatim. Source office: Records IV. Trace by desk.

    Brenava log: 15:50, vehicle approaching, road. 4 pers. O.P.
  13. The car on the road from Kalenov holds a man, a woman, two children and a sheet of paper that is not a grey card. Tomas reads it and hands it back. "I can't take this." The man says it is a hospital letter. Tomas says he can see that. The Standing Order says the bridge, the strip and the train; it says nothing about a road, and nothing is the answer. The bar stays down. The man reverses twenty metres and stops, and then another twenty. The dogs watch the car. Ondra writes the plate and the number of persons and the word returned, which is the word.
    Brenava log: 15:52, vehicle, road, 4 pers. No grey card. Returned. Plate noted. T.B.
  14. Vera uncaps the ink and opens the District Register to the next free line. The pen is the office's; the hand is hers. Serial, year opened, subject, address, status. The line takes eleven seconds and makes no sound but the nib. She blots it. Then the cross-reference, fond S, a codename and a receipt number, so that the one who told is paid. Then the household card, tab turned from pending to complete. She ties the folder with the corridor's double knot and sets it in the out tray, where Berta's eyes will pass over it and not stop. The ledger balances. Nothing in the room has changed except the line.
    Register leaf 212 line 14. IV/4471/R.31 SOKOL Marta, Vrba 9/3. ACTIVE, observation. Ref. fond S/RIBA, rcpt 118.

free tomas_gate
held
  1. A slip arrives in the intake tray before the tea urn is hot: the District Register is to be reconciled in full before the inspection from Central. Every serial a folder, every folder its white. The slip is unsigned, which means the corridor. Berta pins it to the Plan Calendar, and the Plan Calendar says Week 40.
    Ops. IV to Records IV: District Register to be reconciled in full before Central inspection. All serials.
  2. The string tie comes undone in two pulls. Form K-1, then forty leaves numbered in the corner by a hand that changed twice in nine years. Vera reads as the office reads: cover, index, last leaf first. Leaf 40 is a source report, two lines and a foot. A parcel carried up the stair on a Tuesday by a man in a railway coat. Contents stated as medicine, foreign. At the foot, a source and a receipt number. The stair is Vrba Street, number 9; the flat is 3, a widow's. Vera knows the stair. She knows the cough through the wall. She closes the folder on her thumb to keep the place, and the tab stripe is red.
    IV/4471/R.31 leaf 40. Source report, fond S: parcel up stair to Vrba 9/3, Tues., rail staff. Stated: medicine, foreign.
  3. Ten past eleven. The stair light clicks off before she reaches the second gallery and she lets it. Vera knocks at flat 3 the way one knocks after dark, with a knuckle. The chain, the cough, the door. She does not go in. "Pani Sokol. The Tuesday parcel. Not for a while." Marta looks at her the way the building looks at a clerk from the Records Office. "Not on Tuesdays," Vera says, and that is all she brought. Above them, at the third-floor rail, a cigarette is lit and not smoked. The stair light clicks back on without either of them touching it.
    Building book, Vrba 9: 23:10, HALM V. (5) at door of 3, approx. 1 min. No entry. K.
  4. The booth at the Lom post office smells of other people's three minutes. Marta has the Tuesday slot, 18:00. The line hums; her son's voice, then the soft double click two seconds in. She says the weather here is fine. She says: do not send the parcel. Not this month, not the next. She says it twice because the line is loud. He asks about her breath and she says it is her own. The clerk taps the glass. The line stays open half a second after she sets the receiver down. She walks home by Vrba Street slowly, for the stairs, and climbs them stopping twice.
    Lom PO call book: SOKOL M., Vienna, 18:00, 3 min. Tape ref. IV/4471.
  5. The pink carbon goes to the handling officer, the white to Central, the violet stays. Vera has, for one evening, all three on her desk, and the count in the carbon box is Berta's to keep. She folds the violet of leaf 40 into the back of a Plan Calendar sheet, slogan outward, and puts it in her coat. On Vrba Street the cellar hatch is under the chestnut, which the third floor cannot see. She does not go down. She leaves the folded sheet under the bin lid where paper for the press is left, and goes up to flat 5, and runs the tap.
    Carbon box, district: IV/4471/R.31 leaf 40, violet. Count 0 of 1. Checked B.L.
  6. The older signatories want names printed; the wall-writers want none. Jan sets the name himself, so that nobody else has set it. Third floor, front, caretaker since 1984, a telephone in one year instead of eight, a source with a receipt. Beneath it, as proof, the line from a source report, with the receipt number left on, in the state's own wording, serial and all. Four hundred copies. One sheet is read by eight. One of the eight will be the corridor, and the corridor will know which office the serial came from. Jan prints it anyway. The press does not care whose name it is.
    Ops. IV: Lis W40 col. 2 recovered. Quotes IV/4471/R.31 leaf 40 verbatim. Source office: Records IV. Trace by desk.
  7. A car comes down the road from Kalenov, slowly, not the Tuesday train and not the hour for it. A man, a woman, two children, a suitcase tied with a belt. The man holds a sheet of paper out of the window before he reaches the bar. The dogs stand up. The log is open on a knee. ---
    Brenava log: 15:50, vehicle approaching, road. 4 pers. O.P.
  8. The car on the road from Kalenov holds a man, a woman, two children and a sheet of paper that is not a grey card. Tomas reads it and hands it back. "I can't take this." The man says it is a hospital letter. Tomas says he can see that. The Standing Order says the bridge, the strip and the train; it says nothing about a road, and nothing is the answer. The bar stays down. The man reverses twenty metres and stops, and then another twenty. The dogs watch the car. Ondra writes the plate and the number of persons and the word returned, which is the word.
    Brenava log: 15:52, vehicle, road, 4 pers. No grey card. Returned. Plate noted. T.B.
  9. A card arrives at flat 5 by the morning post, faculty crest, typed: the admissions review will sit this week. Date, room, no time. The card has a line for household file, and the line has been filled in by somebody else, in a hand from an office. Vera puts it on the table and Ilona reads it without picking it up.
    Faculty notice: adm. review to sit this week, HALM Ilona. Household file IV/7781/R.40: see attached.
  10. The ambulance takes forty minutes because the gate is locked at 22:00 and the caretaker must be woken. Marta is carried down the stair in her coat by two men who stop twice. The Lom hospital admits her to a corridor bed and puts her on the oxygen it does have. In the morning a nurse with a clipboard asks for the household card, the pharmacy book, and the name of whoever supplies the medicine that is not on the pharmacy's list. Marta says her son writes. The nurse writes that down. The bed has a number. The clipboard has a serial.
    Lom Hospital adm. 03:40: SOKOL M., Vrba 9/3, asthma, acute. Foreign medication noted. Papers requested, SKS IV.
  11. The stove in the banking hall is lit from October. Vera carries the folder across the room at the pace of someone going for tea. Forty leaves, numbered in the corner, go in by fours. The carbons curl first, violet, then white. The K-1 board cover she keeps, because a cover is not a report. Nobody looks up; the urn is loud. Back at the desk the intake log shows a serial with no leaf count beside it, and the initials against that line are not hers. Berta signed the folder in this morning. Vera uncaps her pen and does not write anything.
    Intake log, Mon.: IV/4471/R.31 received, B.L. Leaves: [blank]. Out: [blank].
  12. The review sits in a room at the faculty with a long table and a Plan Calendar. The chair reads the file aloud: name, household, the card from the Records Office with its one line on the back, the marks. The marks are good. A man from the corridor sits at the end of the table and says nothing. The chair says deferred, which is not refused, and pending review, which is what it said before, and the secretary writes it. The letter is typed the same afternoon and says the applicant may apply again in the next cycle. In flat 5 it is read sitting down, once, and left on the table.
    Faculty adm. review, HALM Ilona: DEFERRED, next cycle. Household file IV/7781/R.40: incomplete.
  13. The telephone in flat 5 rings at nine, which is the corridor's hour. The line hums louder than it should. "Comrade Halm. Rybar, Operations." Polite, unhurried, a man with a cup of tea. "Report four-four-seven-one, year thirty-one. It is active and I have the pink. Central does not have the white. Where is it in the Register." A question without a question mark. Vera says she will look in the morning. "The morning, then," he says. "Thank you." The soft double click; the line stays open half a second after she sets it down. Ilona, at the table, has stopped writing.
    Ops. IV, Rybar, call log: HALM V., re IV/4471/R.31, location in Register queried. Reply due a.m.
  14. The violet carbon of leaf 40 is still in the district, because the district keeps everything. Vera signs for the carbon box, finds the source report by serial, and types the leaf back onto office stock through two fresh carbons, with the margin slightly wrong. A folder with a missing leaf is a gap; a folder with a retyped leaf is a folder. She numbers it in the corner in the hand the index already shows, and writes the leaf count into the intake log where the line was blank. Berta's initials stay beside it. The ledger will balance tonight. Vera washes the ink from her thumb.
    Intake log: IV/4471/R.31, leaves 40, reconstituted from district carbon. V.H.

  14. The search has a form and the form has an inventory. Rybar comes down the ladder last, after the two in overalls, and touches nothing. He reads the beam where the tally is pencilled. The press is listed by its maker's plate; the type by the case; the stock by the ream; the sheets by the count. Jan stands by the stove with his hands black and is asked, politely, to sign the inventory as present. He signs. The hatch is sealed with a paper seal that carries the Drawer. The chestnut drops a leaf on it. Jan goes up the ladder between the two in overalls.
    Search inventory, Vrba 9 cellar: platen press (1), type cases (3), stock, sheets. Present: RUSEK J. Sealed.

Jan reads it. It says that he, Jan Rusek, published without licence, that the publication was unauthorised and its contents untrue, that he regrets. It does not ask for names, which is the kindness. He signs. The pen is the state's. It goes through two carbons, white and pink, and the pink stays on the table where he can see it. "Thank you," says Rybar, and means the signature.

  6. The building book sits on the lodge ledge and Kastan writes in it in pencil. Tonight's entry: the hour, the landing, a figure at the door of flat 3 after the gate was barred, how long, which flat the figure went up to. He writes it as he saw it from the third-floor rail: a coat, a knuckle on the door, no light. He does not write what was said, because he did not hear. Thursday he copies the line onto the handler's form and the handler asks nothing. The line goes into a folder whose subject is the widow, and across to a card whose subject is not.
    Source RIBA, W40: 23:10, HALM V. (5) at door of 3, approx. 1 min, no light. Cross-ref. IV/7781/R.40.
  7. Ilona comes down the ladder quicker than the others. Jan waits until the circle has gone up. "Your mother brings work home." It is not a question. "There is a report. A source report, with a serial on it. The violet copy stays in the district. In a drawer, probably. In a kitchen." Ilona says her mother does not bring work home. Jan says all right. Then he says the sheet cannot print a name without the paper behind it, and that the paper is in flat 5. He does not say please. He lets her go up the ladder first and does not watch her go.
    Lis cellar tally: col. 2 held, pending source document (district carbon).

assuming in circle · route watched · rybar vindictive
  1. The list at Brenava is a sheet pinned inside the stamp cabinet, retyped weekly. Rybar adds to it by telephone, reading slowly, and the company clerk types what he reads: the Tuesday international, staff compartment, railway attendants by name, parcels addressed to District IV, Lom. The clerk reads it back. "Thank you," Rybar says, and rings off, and the line stays open half a second. At the gate the sheet goes up with a new line at the bottom and the conscripts read it at the start of the shift the way they read the weather. Seventy kilometres away, a widow's Tuesday has been retyped.
    Brenava list, W40 add.: Tues. intl. train, staff compt., rail attendants: OPEN ALL. Parcels to Lom IV: SEIZE.
  2. The shelf in the cellar holds a tin of ink and no paper. The circle comes down on Tuesday and sits on the crates with nothing to pass round. The press is clean, which is the worst thing a press can be. Someone says the train. Nobody says the name of the man on it.
    Lis cellar tally (beam): stock in, 0. Run, 0.
  3. The Tuesday international is on the bridge at 14:10, nine cars and the staff compartment. The attendant stands in the corridor with his railway card out and a parcel on the shelf behind his head, brown paper, a chemist's string. The dogs are on the platform. The company starts at car one. The log is open on a knee.
    Brenava log, Tues.: 14:10 intl., 9 cars + staff. Inspection begun. O.P.
  4. The staff compartment is last. Marek has his railway card in his hand and the parcel on the shelf behind his head, brown paper, chemist's string. Tomas looks at the card, and at the parcel, and at the parcel. The dogs are on the platform, fed. Ondra is on the step with the log open. "Clear," Tomas says, and stamps the card, and the stamp is the right one. The compartment is not in the log as opened, because it was not opened. The train pulls off the bridge at 14:19. Ondra's pen is still over the line. There is a line in the log with nothing after the time.
    Brenava log, Tues. 14:10 intl.: cars 1-9 insp. Staff compt.: [blank]. O.P.
  5. A car from the Ribbon is at the post by eight. A captain in a civilian coat asks for the log, a room and a cup of tea, in that order, and is given all three. The company stands outside the guardroom in the sand and is called in one at a time, and the ones who come out do not say what was asked.
    4th Bn. Brenava: inquiry convened, gate log W40. All gate personnel to attend. Ops. IV.
  6. The company clerk's door is open in the evenings. Ondra goes in with the log under his arm, sets it down open, and puts a finger by the line with nothing after the time. He says who had the compartment. He says it quietly and once, and gives the minute the train pulled off, which is the kind of detail a clerk likes. The clerk writes it on a form with a serial. Ondra signs beneath as log keeper, which is a job. Back in the hut Tomas is cleaning the stamp. Ondra sits on his bunk and takes his boots off and says nothing about the clerk.
    4th Bn. report, Brenava: staff compt. not inspected, 14:10 intl. Gate: BREN T. Per PETRIK O., log keeper.
  7. The lodge hatch is open and the cigarette on the ledge is the caretaker's. Marta holds the rail. "Pan Kastan." Her breath comes in short sets and he waits with his hands on the ledge. "My son's parcel. Tuesdays. If it did not come up the stair." He says the gate is his, the stair is the cooperative's, and a parcel is not his business. She tells him what he can put in the book instead: the Halm girl, flat 5, evenings, the courtyard, the hatch under the chestnut. He writes nothing while she is there. He takes the cigarette back off the ledge. She goes up, stopping twice.
    Building book, Vrba 9: HALM I. (5), evenings, courtyard, cellar hatch. Per 3. K.
  8. He waits on the second landing with the keys, where the stair is narrow. "Pani Halm." Vera has her bag and her coat. "Your girl. Evenings. The hatch under the chestnut." He says it to the keys. "I haven't put it in the book." He does not say yet, and does not need to; he is a caretaker and she works in records, and both of them know what a book is. He thanks her, for nothing, and goes up to the third floor, and she stands on the landing until the light clicks off, and then presses it.
    Building book, Vrba 9: HALM I. (5), evenings, courtyard. [Not entered.] K.
  9. Two knocks on the hatch, a pause, one knock. Marek comes down the ladder backwards with the bag against his chest, still in the railway coat. On the bench he sets out what the staff compartment carried for the press: two reams of thin Western stock and a tin of ink. The smaller parcel, brown paper and a Vienna chemist's string, stays in his coat. "Flat 3," Marek says. "Before she books the call." Jan weighs the reams the way the press weighs them: four hundred sheets, eight readers a sheet. The cellar has paper again. Marek is already on the ladder, and goes up by the stair. He never sits.
    Lis cellar tally (pencil, beam): stock in, 2 rm. Ink, 1.
  10. The household card for flat 5 has a line for contacts of the household, and the review will not sit until it is filled. Vera fills it. Not her daughter's name; a name the file can use instead. Vrba Street 9, the cellar, the printing. She writes the hatch, the lamp, the hour she has seen light under the chestnut. The pen does not shake. She reads the line as the corridor will read it, and it reads as a clerk doing her work. She turns the tab from pending to complete and ties the string. The card is one line heavier. The cellar is a serial now.
    Household card IV/7781/R.40, HALM, Vrba 9/5. Contacts: RUSEK J., Vrba 9 cellar, unregistered press. COMPLETE.
  11. A card arrives at flat 5 by the morning post, faculty crest, typed: the admissions review will sit this week. Date, room, no time. The card has a line for household file, and the line has been filled in by somebody else, in a hand from an office. Vera puts it on the table and Ilona reads it without picking it up.
    Faculty notice: adm. review to sit this week, HALM Ilona. Household file IV/7781/R.40: see attached.
  12. The review sits in a room at the faculty with a long table and a Plan Calendar. The chair reads the file aloud, which is how a decision is made: name, household, the card from the Records Office with its one line on the back, the Statement of Position if there is one, the marks. The marks are good. A man from the corridor sits at the end of the table, says nothing, and is not introduced. The chair says admitted, the secretary writes it, and the stamp comes down. The letter is typed the same afternoon. In flat 5 it is read standing up, twice, and put in the drawer.
    Faculty adm. review, HALM Ilona: ADMITTED, medical faculty, R.40. File closed, blue tab.
  13. Ilona comes down the ladder quicker than the others. Jan waits until the circle has gone up. "Your mother brings work home." It is not a question. "There is a report. A source report, with a serial on it. The violet copy stays in the district. In a drawer, probably. In a kitchen." Ilona says her mother does not bring work home. Jan says all right. Then he says the sheet cannot print a name without the paper behind it, and that the paper is in flat 5. He does not say please. He lets her go up the ladder first and does not watch her go.
    Lis cellar tally: col. 2 held, pending source document (district carbon).
  14. The search has a form and the form has an inventory. Rybar comes down the ladder last, after the two in overalls, and touches nothing. He reads the beam where the tally is pencilled. The press is listed by its maker's plate; the type by the case; the stock by the ream; the sheets by the count. Jan stands by the stove with his hands black and is asked, politely, to sign the inventory as present. He signs. The hatch is sealed with a paper seal that carries the Drawer. The chestnut drops a leaf on it. Jan goes up the ladder between the two in overalls.
    Search inventory, Vrba 9 cellar: platen press (1), type cases (3), stock, sheets. Present: RUSEK J. Sealed.

Thursday he copies the line onto the handler's form and the handler asks nothing. The line goes into a folder whose subject is the widow, and across to a card whose subject is not.

    Brenava log, Tues. 14:10 intl.: cars 1-9 insp. Staff compt.: [blank]. O.P.
  5. Ilona comes down the ladder quicker than the others. Jan waits until the circle has gone up. "Your mother brings work home." It is not a question. "There is a report. Then he says the sheet cannot print a name without the paper behind it, and that the paper is in flat 5. He does not say please. He lets her go up the ladder first and does not watch her go.
    Lis cellar tally: col. 2 held, pending source document (district carbon).
  6. The kitchen table in flat 5 has one drawer, and the drawer holds the finger-cots her mother brings home by mistake and a folded sheet the colour the state uses for the copy that stays. Ilona reads the serial, the word parcel, the name of the widow through the wall. She reads it twice, because it is her mother's work and her mother's work does not come home. She folds it along its own crease and puts it inside her anatomy notes. The drawer closes with the sound it always makes. Her mother, in the next room, is listening for the time signal.
    Carbon box, district: IV/4471/R.31 leaf 40, violet. Count 0 of 1.
  7. The lodge hatch is open and the cigarette on the ledge is the caretaker's. Marta holds the rail. "Pan Kastan." Her breath comes in short sets and he waits with his hands on the ledge. "My son's parcel. Tuesdays. If it did not come up the stair." He says the gate is his, the stair is the cooperative's, and a parcel is not his business. She tells him what he can put in the book instead: the Halm girl, flat 5, evenings, the courtyard, the hatch under the chestnut. He writes nothing while she is there. He takes the cigarette back off the ledge. She goes up, stopping twice.
    Building book, Vrba 9: HALM I. (5), evenings, courtyard, cellar hatch. Per 3. K.
  8. He waits on the second landing with the keys, where the stair is narrow. "Pani Halm." Vera has her bag and her coat. "Your girl. Evenings. The hatch under the chestnut." He says it to the keys. "I haven't put it in the book." He does not say yet, and does not need to; he is a caretaker and she works in records, and both of them know what a book is. He thanks her, for nothing, and goes up to the third floor, and she stands on the landing until the light clicks off, and then presses it.
    Building book, Vrba 9: HALM I. (5), evenings, courtyard. [Not entered.] K.
  9. Two knocks on the hatch, a pause, one knock. Marek comes down the ladder backwards with the bag against his chest, still in the railway coat. On the bench he sets out what the staff compartment carried for the press: two reams of thin Western stock and a tin of ink. The smaller parcel, brown paper and a Vienna chemist's string, stays in his coat. "Flat 3," Marek says. "Before she books the call." Jan weighs the reams the way the press weighs them: four hundred sheets, eight readers a sheet. The cellar has paper again. Marek is already on the ladder, and goes up by the stair. He never sits.
    Lis cellar tally (pencil, beam): stock in, 2 rm. Ink, 1.
  10. The household card for flat 5 has a line for contacts of the household, and the review will not sit until it is filled. Vera fills it. Not her daughter's name; a name the file can use instead. Vrba Street 9, the cellar, the printing. She writes the hatch, the lamp, the hour she has seen light under the chestnut. The pen does not shake. She reads the line as the corridor will read it, and it reads as a clerk doing her work. She turns the tab from pending to complete and ties the string. The card is one line heavier. The cellar is a serial now.
    Household card IV/7781/R.40, HALM, Vrba 9/5. Contacts: RUSEK J., Vrba 9 cellar, unregistered press. COMPLETE.
  11. A card arrives at flat 5 by the morning post, faculty crest, typed: the admissions review will sit this week. Date, room, no time. The card has a line for household file, and the line has been filled in by somebody else, in a hand from an office. Vera puts it on the table and Ilona reads it without picking it up.
    Faculty notice: adm. review to sit this week, HALM Ilona. Household file IV/7781/R.40: see attached.
  12. The review sits in a room at the faculty with a long table and a Plan Calendar. The chair reads the file aloud, which is how a decision is made: name, household, the card from the Records Office with its one line on the back, the Statement of Position if there is one, the marks. The marks are good. A man from the corridor sits at the end of the table, says nothing, and is not introduced. The chair says admitted, the secretary writes it, and the stamp comes down. The letter is typed the same afternoon. In flat 5 it is read standing up, twice, and put in the drawer.
    Faculty adm. review, HALM Ilona: ADMITTED, medical faculty, R.40. File closed, blue tab.

"Clear," Tomas says, and stamps the card, and the stamp is the right one. The compartment is not in the log as opened, because it was not opened. The train pulls off the bridge at 14:19. Ondra's pen is still over the line. There is a line in the log with nothing after the time.
    Brenava log, Tues. 14:10 intl.: cars 1-9 insp. Staff compt.: [blank]. O.P.
  4. Two knocks on the hatch, a pause, one knock. Marek comes down the ladder backwards with the bag against his chest, still in the railway coat. On the bench he sets out what the staff compartment carried for the press: two reams of thin Western stock and a tin of ink. The smaller parcel, brown paper and a Vienna chemist's string, stays in his coat. "Flat 3," Marek says. "Before she books the call." Jan weighs the reams the way the press weighs them: four hundred sheets, eight readers a sheet. The cellar has paper again. Marek is already on the ladder, and goes up by the stair. He never sits.
    Lis cellar tally (pencil, beam): stock in, 2 rm. Ink, 1.
  5. The building book sits on the lodge ledge and Kastan writes in it in pencil. Tonight's entry: the hour, the landing, a figure at the door of flat 3 after the gate was barred, how long, which flat the figure went up to. He writes it as he saw it from the third-floor rail: a coat, a knuckle on the door, no light. He does not write what was said, because he did not hear. Thursday he copies the line onto the handler's form and the handler asks nothing. The line goes into a folder whose subject is the widow, and across to a card whose subject is not.
    Source RIBA, W40: 23:10, HALM V. (5) at door of 3, approx. 1 min, no light. Cross-ref. IV/7781/R.40.
  6. A car from the Ribbon is at the post by eight. A captain in a civilian coat asks for the log, a room and a cup of tea, in that order, and is given all three. The company stands outside the guardroom in the sand and is called in one at a time, and the ones who come out do not say what was asked.
    4th Bn. Brenava: inquiry convened, gate log W40. All gate personnel to attend. Ops. IV.
  7. The company clerk's door is open in the evenings. Ondra goes in with the log under his arm, sets it down open, and puts a finger by the line with nothing after the time. He says who had the compartment. He says it quietly and once, and gives the minute the train pulled off, which is the kind of detail a clerk likes. The clerk writes it on a form with a serial. Ondra signs beneath as log keeper, which is a job. Back in the hut Tomas is cleaning the stamp. Ondra sits on his bunk and takes his boots off and says nothing about the clerk.
    4th Bn. report, Brenava: staff compt. not inspected, 14:10 intl. Gate: BREN T. Per PETRIK O., log keeper.
  8. Thursday is the meeting. The handler has a corner table at the baths cafe and a receipt book with a carbon. Kastan gives the week: the gate round, who pressed the stair light after ten, which flat has the radio tuned west, who came up the stair with a parcel and on which day. He gives it the way he keeps the building book: by the hour. The handler writes, turns the book, and Kastan signs for a sum that would not buy a coat. The sum is not the point; the signature is. He gets two packets of cigarettes with it, which is the custom, and goes home on tram 11.
    Receipt book IV/S, no. 118: source RIBA, W40, paid, signed. Report filed to IV/4471/R.31 and IV/7781/R.40.
  9. The platen comes down and the house takes the sound through its floor. Jan sets the type by lamp: two columns, the masthead cut from lino, the week's sheet. Ink on the roller, roller on the chase, sheet in, sheet out, the right margin smudged where the roller always runs dry. He stops reading what he prints after the first fifty; the hands know it. Stove cold, lamp low, the tram bell at the loop at half past four. By first light the stack under the beam is four hundred, uneven, inked wrong, people's paper. He wipes his hands on the rag and the hands stay black.
    Lis cellar tally: run 400. Stock out, 1 rm. Sheet W40.
  10. A card arrives at flat 5 by the morning post, faculty crest, typed: the admissions review will sit this week. Date, room, no time. The card has a line for household file, and the line has been filled in by somebody else, in a hand from an office. Vera puts it on the table and Ilona reads it without picking it up.
    Faculty notice: adm. review to sit this week, HALM Ilona. Household file IV/7781/R.40: see attached.
  11. The search has a form and the form has an inventory. Rybar comes down the ladder last, after the two in overalls, and touches nothing. He reads the beam where the tally is pencilled. The press is listed by its maker's plate; the type by the case; the stock by the ream; the sheets by the count. Jan stands by the stove with his hands black and is asked, politely, to sign the inventory as present. He signs. The hatch is sealed with a paper seal that carries the Drawer. The chestnut drops a leaf on it. Jan goes up the ladder between the two in overalls.
    Search inventory, Vrba 9 cellar: platen press (1), type cases (3), stock, sheets. Present: RUSEK J. Sealed.
  12. The review sits in a room at the faculty with a long table and a Plan Calendar. The chair reads the file aloud: name, household, the card from the Records Office with more than one line on the back now, the marks. The marks are good; they are read last, and quickly. A man from the corridor sits at the end of the table and says nothing. The chair says refused, and not eligible to reapply, and the secretary writes it without looking up. The letter is typed the same afternoon. In flat 5 it is read once, folded along the fold it came in, and put back in the envelope.
    Faculty adm. review, HALM Ilona: REFUSED. Household file IV/7781/R.40: adverse. Not eligible to reapply.
  13. The question is asked once, politely, and then the room waits. The inventory from the cellar is on the table: two reams of thin Western stock, a tin of ink, a chemist's string. "The paper is foreign. Somebody carries it." Jan looks at the string for a long time. Then he gives the name that is already on the railway's staff roster and the Tuesday train's duty sheet, where they could have found it in an hour. "Marek. The sleeping car." Rybar writes it in a hand that does not hurry. The string stays on the table. The train is due on the bridge at 14:10.
    Statement RUSEK J., add.: supply via rail staff, Tues. intl. train, attendant MAREK. To list, Brenava.
  14. The pink carbon goes to the handling officer, the white to Central, the violet stays. Vera has, for one evening, all three on her desk, and the count in the carbon box is Berta's to keep. She folds the violet of leaf 40 into the back of a Plan Calendar sheet, slogan outward, and puts it in her coat. On Vrba Street the cellar hatch is under the chestnut, which the third floor cannot see. She does not go down. She leaves the folded sheet under the bin lid where paper for the press is left, and goes up to flat 5, and runs the tap.
    Carbon box, district: IV/4471/R.31 leaf 40, violet. Count 0 of 1. Checked B.L.

  14. The car on the road from Kalenov holds a man, a woman, two children and a sheet of paper that is not a grey card. Tomas reads it and hands it back. "I can't take this." The bar stays down. The man reverses twenty metres and stops, and then another twenty. The dogs watch the car. Ondra writes the plate and the number of persons and the word returned, which is the word.

    Lis cellar tally (pencil, beam): stock in, 2 rm. Ink, 1.
  12. The review sits in a room at the faculty with a long table and a Plan Calendar. The chair reads the file aloud: name, household, the card from the Records Office with its one line on the back, the marks. The marks are good.     Faculty adm. review, HALM Ilona: DEFERRED, next cycle. Household file IV/7781/R.40: incomplete.
  13. Thursday is the meeting. The handler has a corner table at the baths cafe and a receipt book with a carbon. Kastan gives the week: the gate round, who pressed the stair light after ten, which flat has the radio tuned west, who came up the stair with a parcel and on which day. He gives it the way he keeps the building book: by the hour. The handler writes, turns the book, and Kastan signs for a sum that would not buy a coat. The sum is not the point; the signature is. He gets two packets of cigarettes with it, which is the custom, and goes home on tram 11.
    Receipt book IV/S, no. 118: source RIBA, W40, paid, signed. Report filed to IV/4471/R.31 and IV/7781/R.40.
  14. The platen comes down and the house takes the sound through its floor. Jan sets the type by lamp: two columns, the masthead cut from lino, the week's sheet. Ink on the roller, roller on the chase, sheet in, sheet out, the right margin smudged where the roller always runs dry. He stops reading what he prints after the first fifty; the hands know it. Stove cold, lamp low, the tram bell at the loop at half past four. By first light the stack under the beam is four hundred, uneven, inked wrong, people's paper. "Not on Tuesdays," Vera says, and that is all she brought. Above them, at the third-floor rail, a cigarette is lit and not smoked. The stair light clicks back on without either of them touching it.
    Building book, Vrba 9: 23:10, HALM V. (5) at door of 3, approx. 1 min. No entry. K.
  4. The Tuesday international is on the bridge at 14:10, nine cars and the staff compartment. The attendant stands in the corridor with his railway card out and a parcel on the shelf behind his head, brown paper, a chemist's string. The dogs are on the platform. The company starts at car one. The log is open on a knee.
    Brenava log, Tues.: 14:10 intl., 9 cars + staff. Inspection begun. O.P.
  5. The staff compartment is last. Marek has his railway card in his hand and the parcel on the shelf behind his head, brown paper, chemist's string. Tomas looks at the card, and at the parcel, and at the parcel. The dogs are on the platform, fed. Ondra is on the step with the log open. "Clear," Tomas says, and stamps the card, and the stamp is the right one. The compartment is not in the log as opened, because it was not opened. The train pulls off the bridge at 14:19. Ondra's pen is still over the line. There is a line in the log with nothing after the time.
    Brenava log, Tues. 14:10 intl.: cars 1-9 insp. Staff compt.: [blank]. O.P.
  6. The booth at the Lom post office smells of other people's three minutes. Marta has the Tuesday slot, 18:00. The line hums; her son's voice, then the soft double click two seconds in. She says the weather here is fine. She says: do not send the parcel. Not this month, not the next. She says it twice because the line is loud. He asks about her breath and she says it is her own. The clerk taps the glass. The line stays open half a second after she sets the receiver down. She walks home by Vrba Street slowly, for the stairs, and climbs them stopping twice.
    Lom PO call book: SOKOL M., Vienna, 18:00, 3 min. Tape ref. IV/4471.
  7. A car comes down the road from Kalenov, slowly, not the Tuesday train and not the hour for it. A man, a woman, two children, a suitcase tied with a belt. The man holds a sheet of paper out of the window before he reaches the bar. The dogs stand up. The log is open on a knee. ---
    Brenava log: 15:50, vehicle approaching, road. 4 pers. O.P.
  8. The car on the road from Kalenov holds a man, a woman, two children and a sheet of paper that is not a grey card. Tomas reads it and hands it back. "I can't take this." The man says it is a hospital letter. Tomas says he can see that. The Standing Order says the bridge, the strip and the train; it says nothing about a road, and nothing is the answer. The bar stays down. The man reverses twenty metres and stops, and then another twenty. The dogs watch the car. Ondra writes the plate and the number of persons and the word returned, which is the word.
    Brenava log: 15:52, vehicle, road, 4 pers. No grey card. Returned. Plate noted. T.B.
  9. Two knocks on the hatch, a pause, one knock. Marek comes down the ladder backwards with the bag against his chest, still in the railway coat. On the bench he sets out what the staff compartment carried for the press: two reams of thin Western stock and a tin of ink. The smaller parcel, brown paper and a Vienna chemist's string, stays in his coat. "Flat 3," Marek says. "Before she books the call." Jan weighs the reams the way the press weighs them: four hundred sheets, eight readers a sheet. The cellar has paper again. Marek is already on the ladder, and goes up by the stair. He never sits.
    Lis cellar tally (pencil, beam): stock in, 2 rm. Ink, 1.
  10. A card arrives at flat 5 by the morning post, faculty crest, typed: the admissions review will sit this week. Date, room, no time. The card has a line for household file, and the line has been filled in by somebody else, in a hand from an office. Vera puts it on the table and Ilona reads it without picking it up.
    Faculty notice: adm. review to sit this week, HALM Ilona. Household file IV/7781/R.40: see attached.
  11. The review sits in a room at the faculty with a long table and a Plan Calendar. The chair reads the file aloud: name, household, the card from the Records Office with its one line on the back, the marks. The marks are good. A man from the corridor sits at the end of the table and says nothing. The chair says deferred, which is not refused, and pending review, which is what it said before, and the secretary writes it. The letter is typed the same afternoon and says the applicant may apply again in the next cycle. In flat 5 it is read sitting down, once, and left on the table.
    Faculty adm. review, HALM Ilona: DEFERRED, next cycle. Household file IV/7781/R.40: incomplete.
  12. The platen comes down and the house takes the sound through its floor. Jan sets the type by lamp: two columns, the masthead cut from lino, the week's sheet. Ink on the roller, roller on the chase, sheet in, sheet out, the right margin smudged where the roller always runs dry. He stops reading what he prints after the first fifty; the hands know it. Stove cold, lamp low, the tram bell at the loop at half past four. By first light the stack under the beam is four hundred, uneven, inked wrong, people's paper. He wipes his hands on the rag and the hands stay black.
    Lis cellar tally: run 400. Stock out, 1 rm. Sheet W40.
  13. The stove in the banking hall is lit from October. Vera carries the folder across the room at the pace of someone going for tea. Forty leaves, numbered in the corner, go in by fours. The carbons curl first, violet, then white. The K-1 board cover she keeps, because a cover is not a report. Nobody looks up; the urn is loud. Back at the desk the intake log shows a serial with no leaf count beside it, and the initials against that line are not hers. Berta signed the folder in this morning. Vera uncaps her pen and does not write anything.
    Intake log, Mon.: IV/4471/R.31 received, B.L. Leaves: [blank]. Out: [blank].
  14. The form is called a Statement of Position and has a place for a signature and a place for particulars. The particulars are the point. Ilona writes that she attended, that she did not know the nature, that she renounces. Then the line asks where, and the pen stops, and she writes the street, the number, and the word cellar. Her handwriting is her mother's, slightly. The registrar reads it without expression and says the committee can sit again this week. On the stair at home the light clicks off, and she does not press it, and goes up in the dark to flat 5.
    Statement of Position, HALM Ilona: attendance admitted, renounced. Particulars: Vrba 9, cellar, press. Resit.

Kastan gives the week: the gate round, who pressed the stair light after ten, which flat has the radio tuned west, who came up the stair with a parcel and on which day. He gives it the way he keeps the building book: by the hour. The handler writes, turns the book, and Kastan signs for a sum that would not buy a coat. The sum is not the point; the signature is. He gets two packets of cigarettes with it, which is the custom, and goes home on tram 11.
    Receipt book IV/S, no. 118: source RIBA, W40, paid, signed. Report filed to IV/4471/R.31 and IV/7781/R.40.
  11. A card arrives at flat 5 by the morning post, faculty crest, typed: the admissions review will sit this week. Date, room, no time. The card has a line for household file, and the line has been filled in by somebody else, in a hand from an office. Vera puts it on the table and Ilona reads it without picking it up.
    Faculty notice: adm. review to sit this week, HALM Ilona. Household file IV/7781/R.40: see attached.
  12. The review sits in a room at the faculty with a long table and a Plan Calendar. The chair reads the file aloud: name, household, the card from the Records Office with its one line on the back, the marks. The marks are good. A man from the corridor sits at the end of the table and says nothing. The chair says deferred, which is not refused, and pending review, which is what it said before, and the secretary writes it. The letter is typed the same afternoon and says the applicant may apply again in the next cycle. In flat 5 it is read sitting down, once, and left on the table.
    Faculty adm. review, HALM Ilona: DEFERRED, next cycle. Household file IV/7781/R.40: incomplete.
  13. The search has a form and the form has an inventory. Rybar comes down the ladder last, after the two in overalls, and touches nothing. He reads the beam where the tally is pencilled. The press is listed by its maker's plate; the type by the case; the stock by the ream; the sheets by the count. Jan stands by the stove with his hands black and is asked, politely, to sign the inventory as present. He signs. The hatch is sealed with a paper seal that carries the Drawer. The chestnut drops a leaf on it. Jan goes up the ladder between the two in overalls.
    Search inventory, Vrba 9 cellar: platen press (1), type cases (3), stock, sheets. Present: RUSEK J. Sealed.
  14. The lodge hatch is open and the cigarette on the ledge is the caretaker's. Marta holds the rail. "Pan Kastan." Her breath comes in short sets and he waits with his hands on the ledge. "My son's parcel. Tuesdays. If it did not come up the stair." He says the gate is his, the stair is the cooperative's, and a parcel is not his business. She tells him what he can put in the book instead: the Halm girl, flat 5, evenings, the courtyard, the hatch under the chestnut. He writes nothing while she is there. He takes the cigarette back off the ledge. She goes up, stopping twice.
    Building book, Vrba 9: HALM I. (5), evenings, courtyard, cellar hatch. Per 3. K.

  1. The admissions file for the medical faculty is a thin folder with a blue tab and a card clipped to the front.     Ops. IV to Records IV: District Register to be reconciled in full before Central inspection. All serials.
  3. The Tuesday international is on the bridge at 14:10, nine cars and the staff compartment. The attendant stands in the corridor with his railway card out and a parcel on the shelf behind his head, brown paper, a chemist's string. The dogs are on the platform. The company starts at car one. The log is open on a knee.
    Brenava log, Tues.: 14:10 intl., 9 cars + staff. Inspection begun. O.P.
  4. The string tie comes undone in two pulls. Form K-1, then forty leaves numbered in the corner by a hand that changed twice in nine years. Vera reads as the office reads: cover, index, last leaf first. Leaf 40 is a source report, two lines and a foot. A parcel carried up the stair on a Tuesday by a man in a railway coat. Contents stated as medicine, foreign. At the foot, a source and a receipt number. The stair is Vrba Street, number 9; the flat is 3, a widow's. Vera knows the stair. She knows the cough through the wall. She closes the folder on her thumb to keep the place, and the tab stripe is red.
    IV/4471/R.31 leaf 40. Source report, fond S: parcel up stair to Vrba 9/3, Tues., rail staff. Stated: medicine, foreign.
  5. The staff compartment is last. Marek has his railway card in his hand and the parcel on the shelf behind his head, brown paper, chemist's string. Tomas looks at the card, and at the parcel, and at the parcel. The dogs are on the platform, fed. Ondra is on the step with the log open. "Clear," Tomas says, and stamps the card, and the stamp is the right one. The compartment is not in the log as opened, because it was not opened. The train pulls off the bridge at 14:19. Ondra's pen is still over the line. There is a line in the log with nothing after the time.
    Brenava log, Tues. 14:10 intl.: cars 1-9 insp. Staff compt.: [blank]. O.P.
  6. A car from the Ribbon is at the post by eight. A captain in a civilian coat asks for the log, a room and a cup of tea, in that order, and is given all three. The company stands outside the guardroom in the sand and is called in one at a time, and the ones who come out do not say what was asked.
    4th Bn. Brenava: inquiry convened, gate log W40. All gate personnel to attend. Ops. IV.
  7. The captain is polite. He lays the log on the table between them, open at the line with nothing after the time, and does not point. "I'm not interested in the line," he says. "I'm interested in what comes through it." Ondra is at the door with his cap under his arm. Tomas has seen the parcel on the shelf, the chemist's string, the railway card. He says what the parcel was, whose coat carried it, and which day of the week. The captain writes it down and underlines the day. The log closes. Ondra is told to go back to the stool. Nobody says his name again.
    4th Bn. report, Brenava: supply route: Tues. intl. train, rail staff, parcels, Vienna. Log clerk cleared.
  8. Two knocks on the hatch, a pause, one knock. Marek comes down the ladder backwards with the bag against his chest, still in the railway coat. On the bench he sets out what the staff compartment carried for the press: two reams of thin Western stock and a tin of ink. The smaller parcel, brown paper and a Vienna chemist's string, stays in his coat. "Flat 3," Marek says. "Before she books the call." Jan weighs the reams the way the press weighs them: four hundred sheets, eight readers a sheet. The cellar has paper again. Marek is already on the ladder, and goes up by the stair. He never sits.
    Lis cellar tally (pencil, beam): stock in, 2 rm. Ink, 1.
  9. The platen comes down and the house takes the sound through its floor. Jan sets the type by lamp: two columns, the masthead cut from lino, the week's sheet. Ink on the roller, roller on the chase, sheet in, sheet out, the right margin smudged where the roller always runs dry. He stops reading what he prints after the first fifty; the hands know it. Stove cold, lamp low, the tram bell at the loop at half past four. By first light the stack under the beam is four hundred, uneven, inked wrong, people's paper. He wipes his hands on the rag and the hands stay black.
    Lis cellar tally: run 400. Stock out, 1 rm. Sheet W40.
  10. A card arrives at flat 5 by the morning post, faculty crest, typed: the admissions review will sit this week. Date, room, no time.     Faculty notice: adm. review to sit this week, HALM Ilona. Household file IV/7781/R.40: see attached.

The chair reads the file aloud: name, household, the card from the Records Office with its one line on the back, the marks. The marks are good. A man from the corridor sits at the end of the table and says nothing. The chair says deferred, which is not refused, and pending review, which is what it said before, and the secretary writes it. The letter is typed the same afternoon and says the applicant may apply again in the next cycle. In flat 5 it is read sitting down, once, and left on the table.
    Faculty adm. review, HALM Ilona: DEFERRED, next cycle. Household file IV/7781/R.40: incomplete.
  12. The stove in the banking hall is lit from October. Vera carries the folder across the room at the pace of someone going for tea. Forty leaves, numbered in the corner, go in by fours. The carbons curl first, violet, then white. The K-1 board cover she keeps, because a cover is not a report. Nobody looks up; the urn is loud. Back at the desk the intake log shows a serial with no leaf count beside it, and the initials against that line are not hers. Berta signed the folder in this morning. Vera uncaps her pen and does not write anything.
    Intake log, Mon.: IV/4471/R.31 received, B.L. Leaves: [blank]. Out: [blank].
  13. She comes down with the others and Jan is at the foot of the ladder before she reaches the bottom rung. "Not you. Not any more." He says it to the wall above her head. "Go up, and go home by the street, not the yard." She asks why, once. He has a reason and does not give it, because a reason is a thing that can be repeated. The circle behind him pretends to count sheets. The hatch comes down. On the gallery she stands a moment with the courtyard lamp on her and the third-floor rail empty, then goes up to flat 5 by the stair, as told.
    Lis cellar tally: circle, W40: 3. (Struck: 4.)
  14. The intake log has a line with a serial and nothing after it, and the initials beside the line are Berta's. Vera does not strike anything; the Register is not opened. She takes the pen from the dish by the finger-cots, Berta's pen, and fills the line in a hand close enough to Berta's: leaves, forty; out, to handling officer; the initials again, B.L. Nine years at the next desk is long enough to learn a loop. The log now says a folder came in whole and went out whole, and the name on both ends of the line is not hers. She blots it and sets the pen back in the dish. Across the desk Berta is counting a blue tab and does not look up.
    Intake log, Mon.: IV/4471/R.31 received B.L. Leaves 40. Out: to H.O. B.L.

    Building book, Vrba 9: 23:10, HALM V. (5) at door of 3, approx. 1 min. No entry. K.
  4. The booth at the Lom post office smells of other people's three minutes. Marta has the Tuesday slot, 18:00. The line hums; her son's voice, then the soft double click two seconds in. The clerk taps the glass. The line stays open half a second after she sets the receiver down. She walks home by Vrba Street slowly, for the stairs, and climbs them stopping twice.
    Lom PO call book: SOKOL M., Vienna, 18:00, 3 min. Tape ref. IV/4471.
  5. The pink carbon goes to the handling officer, the white to Central, the violet stays. Vera has, for one evening, all three on her desk, and the count in the carbon box is Berta's to keep. On Vrba Street the cellar hatch is under the chestnut, which the third floor cannot see. She does not go down.     Carbon box, district: IV/4471/R.31 leaf 40, violet. Count 0 of 1. Checked B.L.
  6. The older signatories want names printed; the wall-writers want none. Jan sets the name himself, so that nobody else has set it. Third floor, front, caretaker since 1984, a telephone in one year instead of eight, a source with a receipt.     Brenava log: 15:50, vehicle approaching, road. 4 pers. O.P.
  8. The car on the road from Kalenov holds a man, a woman, two children and a sheet of paper that is not a grey card. Tomas reads it and hands it back. "I can't take this." The bar stays down. The man reverses twenty metres and stops, and then another twenty. The dogs watch the car. Ondra writes the plate and the number of persons and the word returned, which is the word.
    Brenava log: 15:52, vehicle, road, 4 pers. No grey card. Returned. Plate noted. T.B.
  9. A card arrives at flat 5 by the morning post, faculty crest, typed: the admissions review will sit this week. Date, room, no time. The card has a line for household file, and the line has been filled in by somebody else, in a hand from an office. Vera puts it on the table and Ilona reads it without picking it up.
    Faculty notice: adm. review to sit this week, HALM Ilona. Household file IV/7781/R.40: see attached.
  10. The review sits in a room at the faculty with a long table and a Plan Calendar. The chair reads the file aloud: name, household, the card from the Records Office with its one line on the back, the marks. The marks are good. A man from the corridor sits at the end of the table and says nothing. The chair says deferred, which is not refused, and pending review, which is what it said before, and the secretary writes it. The letter is typed the same afternoon and says the applicant may apply again in the next cycle. In flat 5 it is read sitting down, once, and left on the table.
    Faculty adm. review, HALM Ilona: DEFERRED, next cycle. Household file IV/7781/R.40: incomplete.
  11. The ambulance takes forty minutes because the gate is locked at 22:00 and the caretaker must be woken. Marta is carried down the stair in her coat by two men who stop twice. In the morning a nurse with a clipboard asks for the household card, the pharmacy book, and the name of whoever supplies the medicine that is not on the pharmacy's list. Marta says her son writes. The nurse writes that down. The bed has a number. The clipboard has a serial.
    Lom Hospital adm. 03:40: SOKOL M., Vrba 9/3, asthma, acute. Foreign medication noted. Papers requested, SKS IV.
  12. The stove in the banking hall is lit from October. Vera carries the folder across the room at the pace of someone going for tea. Forty leaves, numbered in the corner, go in by fours. Back at the desk the intake log shows a serial with no leaf count beside it, and the initials against that line are not hers. Berta signed the folder in this morning. Vera uncaps her pen and does not write anything.
    Intake log, Mon.: IV/4471/R.31 received, B.L. Leaves: [blank]. Out: [blank].
  13. The intake log has a line with a serial and nothing after it, and the initials beside the line are Berta's. Vera does not strike anything; the Register is not opened. Nine years at the next desk is long enough to learn a loop. The log now says a folder came in whole and went out whole, and the name on both ends of the line is not hers. She blots it and sets the pen back in the dish. Across the desk Berta is counting a blue tab and does not look up.
    Intake log, Mon.: IV/4471/R.31 received B.L. Leaves 40. Out: to H.O. B.L.

    Brenava log, Tues. 14:10 intl.: cars 1-9 insp. Staff compt.: [blank]. O.P.

    4th Bn. Brenava: inquiry convened, gate log W40. All gate personnel to attend. Ops. IV.
  6. The company clerk's door is open in the evenings. Ondra goes in with the log under his arm, sets it down open, and puts a finger by the line with nothing after the time. Ondra signs beneath as log keeper, which is a job. Back in the hut Tomas is cleaning the stamp. Ondra sits on his bunk and takes his boots off and says nothing about the clerk.
    4th Bn. report, Brenava: staff compt. not inspected, 14:10 intl. Gate: BREN T. Per PETRIK O., log keeper.
