  2. The Tuesday international is on the bridge at 14:10, nine cars and the staff compartment. The attendant stands in the corridor with his railway card out and a parcel on the shelf behind his head, brown paper, a chemist's string. The dogs are on the platform. The company starts at car one. The log is open on a knee.
    Brenava log, Tues.: 14:10 intl., 9 cars + staff. Inspection begun. O.P.
  3. The staff compartment is last. Marek has his railway card in his hand and the parcel on the shelf behind his head, brown paper, chemist's string. Tomas looks at the card, and at the parcel, and at the parcel. The dogs are on the platform, fed. Ondra is on the step with the log open. "Clear," Tomas says, and stamps the card, and the stamp is the right one. The compartment is not in the log as opened, because it was not opened. The train pulls off the bridge at 14:19. Ondra's pen is still over the line. There is a line in the log with nothing after the time.
    Brenava log, Tues. 14:10 intl.: cars 1-9 insp. Staff compt.: [blank]. O.P.
  4. The string tie comes undone in two pulls. Form K-1, then forty leaves numbered in the corner by a hand that changed twice in nine years. Vera reads as the office reads: cover, index, last leaf first. Leaf 40 is a source report, two lines and a foot. A parcel carried up the stair on a Tuesday by a man in a railway coat. Contents stated as medicine, foreign. At the foot, a source and a receipt number. The stair is Vrba Street, number 9; the flat is 3, a widow's. Vera knows the stair. She knows the cough through the wall. She closes the folder on her thumb to keep the place, and the tab stripe is red.
    IV/4471/R.31 leaf 40. Source report, fond S: parcel up stair to Vrba 9/3, Tues., rail staff. Stated: medicine, foreign.
  5. A car from the Ribbon is at the post by eight. A captain in a civilian coat asks for the log, a room and a cup of tea, in that order, and is given all three. The company stands outside the guardroom in the sand and is called in one at a time, and the ones who come out do not say what was asked.
    4th Bn. Brenava: inquiry convened, gate log W40. All gate personnel to attend. Ops. IV.
  6. The captain reads the log the way the Ribbon reads: last page first. "This line." Tomas can see it upside down: the time, and nothing after. Ondra's hand. Ondra stands at the guardroom door with his cap under his arm, nineteen, with a father at the depot and an uncle who is a mark on a card. "Mine," Tomas says. "I had the compartment. I called it clear and he wrote what I called." The captain nods, which is not agreement, and writes. The report form has room for one name. Tomas watches the pen put his there, and not Ondra's.
    4th Bn. report, Brenava: staff compt. not inspected, 14:10 intl. Responsible: BREN T., pte. Log clerk cleared.
  7. The lodge hatch is open and the cigarette on the ledge is the caretaker's. Marta holds the rail. "Pan Kastan." Her breath comes in short sets and he waits with his hands on the ledge. "My son's parcel. Tuesdays. If it did not come up the stair." He says the gate is his, the stair is the cooperative's, and a parcel is not his business. She tells him what he can put in the book instead: the Halm girl, flat 5, evenings, the courtyard, the hatch under the chestnut. He writes nothing while she is there. He takes the cigarette back off the ledge. She goes up, stopping twice.
    Building book, Vrba 9: HALM I. (5), evenings, courtyard, cellar hatch. Per 3. K.
  8. He waits on the second landing with the keys, where the stair is narrow. "Pani Halm." Vera has her bag and her coat. "Your girl. Evenings. The hatch under the chestnut." He says it to the keys. "I haven't put it in the book." He does not say yet, and does not need to; he is a caretaker and she works in records, and both of them know what a book is. He thanks her, for nothing, and goes up to the third floor, and she stands on the landing until the light clicks off, and then presses it.
    Building book, Vrba 9: HALM I. (5), evenings, courtyard. [Not entered.] K.
  9. Two knocks on the hatch, a pause, one knock. Marek comes down the ladder backwards with the bag against his chest, still in the railway coat. On the bench he sets out what the staff compartment carried for the press: two reams of thin Western stock and a tin of ink. The smaller parcel, brown paper and a Vienna chemist's string, stays in his coat. "Flat 3," Marek says. "Before she books the call." Jan weighs the reams the way the press weighs them: four hundred sheets, eight readers a sheet. The cellar has paper again. Marek is already on the ladder, and goes up by the stair. He never sits.
    Lis cellar tally (pencil, beam): stock in, 2 rm. Ink, 1.
  10. A card arrives at flat 5 by the morning post, faculty crest, typed: the admissions review will sit this week. Date, room, no time. The card has a line for household file, and the line has been filled in by somebody else, in a hand from an office. Vera puts it on the table and Ilona reads it without picking it up.
    Faculty notice: adm. review to sit this week, HALM Ilona. Household file IV/7781/R.40: see attached.
  11. The household card for flat 5 has a line for contacts of the household, and the review will not sit until it is filled. Vera fills it. Not her daughter's name; a name the file can use instead. Vrba Street 9, the cellar, the printing. She writes the hatch, the lamp, the hour she has seen light under the chestnut. The pen does not shake. She reads the line as the corridor will read it, and it reads as a clerk doing her work. She turns the tab from pending to complete and ties the string. The card is one line heavier. The cellar is a serial now.
    Household card IV/7781/R.40, HALM, Vrba 9/5. Contacts: RUSEK J., Vrba 9 cellar, unregistered press. COMPLETE.
  12. The platen comes down and the house takes the sound through its floor. Jan sets the type by lamp: two columns, the masthead cut from lino, the week's sheet. Ink on the roller, roller on the chase, sheet in, sheet out, the right margin smudged where the roller always runs dry. He stops reading what he prints after the first fifty; the hands know it. Stove cold, lamp low, the tram bell at the loop at half past four. By first light the stack under the beam is four hundred, uneven, inked wrong, people's paper. He wipes his hands on the rag and the hands stay black.
    Lis cellar tally: run 400. Stock out, 1 rm. Sheet W40.
  13. The sheets go out the way they always go: folded into Delnik under doormats, under the seats of tram 11 on the loop run, in the lockers at the baths, through the parcel counter. Jan takes Lom himself, landing by landing, one sheet a floor, the stair lights clicking off behind him every ninety seconds. He does not look at who reads. By the evening programme a sheet is being read aloud through a wall somewhere, badly. By Thursday the Vienna transmitter reads it in a better voice.
    4th Bn. order of the day: post sacks and staff compts. opened in full. Reason: hostile print in circulation.
  14. The review sits in a room at the faculty with a long table and a Plan Calendar. The chair reads the file aloud, which is how a decision is made: name, household, the card from the Records Office with its one line on the back, the Statement of Position if there is one, the marks. The marks are good. A man from the corridor sits at the end of the table, says nothing, and is not introduced. The chair says admitted, the secretary writes it, and the stamp comes down. The letter is typed the same afternoon. In flat 5 it is read standing up, twice, and put in the drawer.
    Faculty adm. review, HALM Ilona: ADMITTED, medical faculty, R.40. File closed, blue tab.

  10. The room at the Ribbon has a table, two chairs and a typewriter whose sample page is on file. Rybar does not raise his voice; he has not needed to. The declaration is already typed. Jan reads it. It says that he, Jan Rusek, published without licence, that the publication was unauthorised and its contents untrue, that he regrets. It does not ask for names, which is the kindness. He signs. The pen is the state's. It goes through two carbons, white and pink, and the pink stays on the table where he can see it. "Thank you," says Rybar, and means the signature.
    Declaration, RUSEK Jan: publication unlicensed, contents untrue. Regret expressed. Signed. Copies 2.
  11. The pink carbon goes to the handling officer, the white to Central, the violet stays. Vera has, for one evening, all three on her desk, and the count in the carbon box is Berta's to keep. She folds the violet of leaf 40 into the back of a Plan Calendar sheet, slogan outward, and puts it in her coat. On Vrba Street the cellar hatch is under the chestnut, which the third floor cannot see. She does not go down. She leaves the folded sheet under the bin lid where paper for the press is left, and goes up to flat 5, and runs the tap.
    Carbon box, district: IV/4471/R.31 leaf 40, violet. Count 0 of 1. Checked B.L.
  12. The review sits in a room at the faculty with a long table and a Plan Calendar. The chair reads the file aloud: name, household, the card from the Records Office with more than one line on the back now, the marks. The marks are good; they are read last, and quickly. A man from the corridor sits at the end of the table and says nothing. The chair says refused, and not eligible to reapply, and the secretary writes it without looking up. The letter is typed the same afternoon. In flat 5 it is read once, folded along the fold it came in, and put back in the envelope.
    Faculty adm. review, HALM Ilona: REFUSED. Household file IV/7781/R.40: adverse. Not eligible to reapply.
  13. Berta's memos are typed, because her hand is known. Subject: intake, District Register, discrepancy. Serial as above. It gives no name; in this office a desk is a name. She reads it once, pulls the carbon, and puts the white in the registrar's tray beneath a blue-tab count, where it will be found in the course of things. She does not look across. Four years from pension. She sharpens the pencil.
    Memo, Records IV, W40: intake discrepancy, IV/4471/R.31. Folder to desk 2. No leaf count. B.L.
  14. The stove in the banking hall is lit from October. Vera carries the folder across the room at the pace of someone going for tea. Forty leaves, numbered in the corner, go in by fours. The carbons curl first, violet, then white. The K-1 board cover she keeps, because a cover is not a report. Nobody looks up; the urn is loud. Back at the desk the intake log shows a serial with no leaf count beside it, and the initials against that line are not hers. Berta signed the folder in this morning. Vera uncaps her pen and does not write anything.
    Intake log, Mon.: IV/4471/R.31 received, B.L. Leaves: [blank]. Out: [blank].

Jan stands by the stove with his hands black and is asked, politely, to sign the inventory as present. He signs. The hatch is sealed with a paper seal that carries the Drawer. The chestnut drops a leaf on it. Jan goes up the ladder between the two in overalls.
    Search inventory, Vrba 9 cellar: platen press (1), type cases (3), stock, sheets. Present: RUSEK J. Sealed.
  7. The question is asked once, politely, and then the room waits. The inventory from the cellar is on the table: two reams of thin Western stock, a tin of ink, a chemist's string. "The paper is foreign. Somebody carries it." Jan looks at the string for a long time. Then he gives the name that is already on the railway's staff roster and the Tuesday train's duty sheet, where they could have found it in an hour. "Marek. The sleeping car." Rybar writes it in a hand that does not hurry. The string stays on the table. The train is due on the bridge at 14:10.
    Statement RUSEK J., add.: supply via rail staff, Tues. intl. train, attendant MAREK. To list, Brenava.
  8. The room at the Ribbon has a table, two chairs and a typewriter whose sample page is on file. Rybar does not raise his voice; he has not needed to. The declaration is already typed. Jan reads it. It says that he, Jan Rusek, published without licence, that the publication was unauthorised and its contents untrue, that he regrets. It does not ask for names, which is the kindness. He signs. The pen is the state's. It goes through two carbons, white and pink, and the pink stays on the table where he can see it. "Thank you," says Rybar, and means the signature.
    Declaration, RUSEK Jan: publication unlicensed, contents untrue. Regret expressed. Signed. Copies 2.
  9. Two knocks on the hatch, a pause, one knock. Marek comes down the ladder backwards with the bag against his chest, still in the railway coat. On the bench he sets out what the staff compartment carried for the press: two reams of thin Western stock and a tin of ink. The smaller parcel, brown paper and a Vienna chemist's string, stays in his coat. "Flat 3," Marek says. "Before she books the call." Jan weighs the reams the way the press weighs them: four hundred sheets, eight readers a sheet. The cellar has paper again. Marek is already on the ladder, and goes up by the stair. He never sits.
    Lis cellar tally (pencil, beam): stock in, 2 rm. Ink, 1.
  10. A card arrives at flat 5 by the morning post, faculty crest, typed: the admissions review will sit this week. Date, room, no time. The card has a line for household file, and the line has been filled in by somebody else, in a hand from an office. Vera puts it on the table and Ilona reads it without picking it up.
    Faculty notice: adm. review to sit this week, HALM Ilona. Household file IV/7781/R.40: see attached.
  11. The stove in the banking hall is lit from October. Vera carries the folder across the room at the pace of someone going for tea. Forty leaves, numbered in the corner, go in by fours. The carbons curl first, violet, then white. The K-1 board cover she keeps, because a cover is not a report. Nobody looks up; the urn is loud. Back at the desk the intake log shows a serial with no leaf count beside it, and the initials against that line are not hers. Berta signed the folder in this morning. Vera uncaps her pen and does not write anything.
    Intake log, Mon.: IV/4471/R.31 received, B.L. Leaves: [blank]. Out: [blank].
  12. The intake log has a line with a serial and nothing after it, and the initials beside the line are Berta's. Vera does not strike anything; the Register is not opened. She takes the pen from the dish by the finger-cots, Berta's pen, and fills the line in a hand close enough to Berta's: leaves, forty; out, to handling officer; the initials again, B.L. Nine years at the next desk is long enough to learn a loop. The log now says a folder came in whole and went out whole, and the name on both ends of the line is not hers. She blots it and sets the pen back in the dish. Across the desk Berta is counting a blue tab and does not look up.
    Intake log, Mon.: IV/4471/R.31 received B.L. Leaves 40. Out: to H.O. B.L.
  13. Berta's memos are typed, because her hand is known. Subject: intake, District Register, discrepancy. Serial as above. The memo says what the log says: a folder signed in, no leaf count against it, no out time, the initials beside the line hers. It says which desk the folder went to. It gives no name; in this office a desk is a name. She reads it once, pulls the carbon, and puts the white in the registrar's tray beneath a blue-tab count, where it will be found in the course of things. She does not look across. Four years from pension. She sharpens the pencil.
    Memo, Records IV, W40: intake discrepancy, IV/4471/R.31. Folder to desk 2. No leaf count. B.L.
  14. The review sits in a room at the faculty with a long table and a Plan Calendar. The chair reads the file aloud, which is how a decision is made: name, household, the card from the Records Office with its one line on the back, the Statement of Position if there is one, the marks. The marks are good. A man from the corridor sits at the end of the table, says nothing, and is not introduced. The chair says admitted, the secretary writes it, and the stamp comes down. The letter is typed the same afternoon. In flat 5 it is read standing up, twice, and put in the drawer.
    Faculty adm. review, HALM Ilona: ADMITTED, medical faculty, R.40. File closed, blue tab.

  1. The admissions file for the medical faculty is a thin folder with a blue tab and a card clipped to the front. Rybar unclips the card and writes on the back, in the corridor's hand, one line: review held pending completion of household file, Records IV. He initials it and clips it back. He telephones nobody. The card goes back to the faculty by the morning courier, and the faculty files it, and the faculty secretary types a note to the applicant's mother's address, which is also the applicant's. The note arrives on a Tuesday. It is very short and it says pending.
    Faculty adm. card, HALM Ilona: REVIEW HELD, pending completion of household file IV/7781/R.40, Records IV. R.
  2. A slip arrives in the intake tray before the tea urn is hot: the District Register is to be reconciled in full before the inspection from Central. Every serial a folder, every folder its white. The slip is unsigned, which means the corridor. Berta pins it to the Plan Calendar, and the Plan Calendar says Week 40.
    Ops. IV to Records IV: District Register to be reconciled in full before Central inspection. All serials.
  3. The form is called a Statement of Position and has a place for a signature and a place for particulars. The particulars are the point. Ilona writes that she attended, that she did not know the nature, that she renounces. Then the line asks where, and the pen stops, and she writes the street, the number, and the word cellar. Her handwriting is her mother's, slightly. The registrar reads it without expression and says the committee can sit again this week. On the stair at home the light clicks off, and she does not press it, and goes up in the dark to flat 5.
    Statement of Position, HALM Ilona: attendance admitted, renounced. Particulars: Vrba 9, cellar, press. Resit.
  4. The Tuesday international is on the bridge at 14:10, nine cars and the staff compartment. The attendant stands in the corridor with his railway card out and a parcel on the shelf behind his head, brown paper, a chemist's string. The dogs are on the platform. The company starts at car one. The log is open on a knee.
    Brenava log, Tues.: 14:10 intl., 9 cars + staff. Inspection begun. O.P.

Contents stated as medicine, foreign. At the foot, a source and a receipt number. The stair is Vrba Street, number 9; the flat is 3, a widow's. Vera knows the stair. She knows the cough through the wall. She closes the folder on her thumb to keep the place, and the tab stripe is red.
    IV/4471/R.31 leaf 40. Source report, fond S: parcel up stair to Vrba 9/3, Tues., rail staff. Stated: medicine, foreign.
